instruction: Download the image from "https://huggingface.co/datasets/xlangai/ubuntu_osworld_file_cache/resolve/main/multi_apps/3c8f201a-009d-4bbe-8b65-a6f8b35bb57f/kingbird.jpeg" and compress it to under 400KB as "low_quality.jpeg" on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires downloading image and compressing to under 400KB. Using existing check_image_file_size metric from the official GIMP metrics library.

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator correctly verifies the primary requirement: file size under 400KB
The getter extracts the correct file from the correct location (/home/user/Desktop/low_quality.jpeg)
The metric logic correctly compares file size against the threshold using os.path.getsize()
Expected value (400000 bytes) semantically matches the instruction requirement (under 400KB)
Edge cases (missing file, wrong size) are handled correctly - returns 0.0 for failures
No postconfig needed as file operations persist to disk
Minor limitation: doesn't verify the image content or download source, but this is acceptable given the instruction focuses on compression
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Could add a check to verify the file is actually an image format (JPEG) using file extension or magic bytes
Could optionally verify image content similarity to source using structure comparison, but this may be overkill for a compression task
